findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there wasn’t an employee present who was food manager certified. Discussed getting at least one more individual food manger certified to ensure that all hours of operation are covered.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed at least two home made sauces stored at room temperature along the cookline. The PIC mentioned that the sauces are pulled from the cooler as needed. Discussed if wanting to keep sauces on counter that the facility will need to use time control for safety of the sauces. Time/Temperature (TCS) foods must either be refrigerated when not in use or placed on time control for up to four hours and then discarded. In the future, the facility will use time control or place sauces on ice bath for temperature control.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: After two cycles, the dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm. It appeared that the sanitizer bucket was empty. The person-in-charge replaced the bucket and the machine was retested at 100ppm (CL). Violation corrected on site. Be sure to monitor levels of sanitizer buckets to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly, as this helps to maximize the effectiveness against the spread of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Both soda guns in the bar area were observed with dried liquid debris on the inner surfaces (inside nozzles). Shown to the PIC and the surfaces were sanitized during the visit to correct the violation. The facility mentioned that the nozzles are cleaned every night. Suggested wiping the surfaces with a sanitizer towel to remove debris from hard to reach places. Ensure that the surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Various Time/Temperature Control (TCS) foods were observed without proper date marking. These items included many white sauces, cooked shrimps, and cheese sauce. Shown to the PIC and the sauces were marked with the preparation date and the shrimps were discarded. Violation corrected. Ensure that all TCS Foods that will be held in house overnight are date marked and discarded if held longer than seven days after preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, there weren’t any sanitizer buckets available throughout the kitchen. The kitchen was in full service and was in the midst of preparing food. Discussed with the PIC and two sanitizer buckets were prepared for both the pizza and grill station. Each bucket tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always available during food prep to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed a container of cooked noodles to be stored on a counter to the right of the hood system. The noodles were tempted at 76F and were discarded by the PIC. PIC mentioned that the noodles must’ve been left on the counter from lunch and that the noodles are normally stored in the cooler. Be sure that noodles are held at 41F or below and never on the counter when not in use. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a gallon of whole milk to be out of date in the standing cooler. The manufacturer’s use-by-date was 4/1/2024. Milk was pulled from cooler and was discarded. Ensure that TCS food does not exceed the manufacturer’s use by date. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlabeled spray bottle observed among the chemicals stored under the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the bottle to indicate its contents (degreaser).
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 1) Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on debris. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during inspection. 
2) Food debris was observed along the blade on the back side of the slicer. GM noted slicer was not used during the current operating day. Slicer was disassembled to be cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 4-302.13 Facility has a heat sanitizing dish machine and does not currently have an irreversible registering temperature indicator for checking the surface temperature at the dishes during a ware washing cycle. Options for dish machine temperature test strips and maximum registering thermometers were discussed. Dish temp tester was ordered during inspection and is scheduled to arrive within 2 to 5 business days. Picture of functioning dish temp tester will be sent to inspector once it is available for use at the facility. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Seal the triple sink to the wall/secure all sinks to the wall. Seal tops of the short walls - in-process during inspection.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Seal bare wood wall border with stain or paint by next routine inspection.
